subject: Novaflow: request for remediation after multi-hour latency spike
messages:
From: Aditi Sharma <aditi@novaflow.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: support@novaflow.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: High tail latency on 2027-06-27 — ask for remediation credit

Jonas,

We saw a significant tail-latency event yesterday (2027-06-27) in our production traffic between ~03:15–03:50 UTC. P95 latency for our inference calls spiked to ~1.2s (baseline ~180ms) and impacted ~18% of requests during the window. This caused a visible degradation in user experience on our web tier and triggered retries that increased downstream costs.

Attached is our collection of traces and the anonymized request IDs we captured (novaflow_latency_report_0627.pdf). Our contract references a P95 objective that this incident clearly violated, and we need to understand what happened and what remediation you propose.

Specifically:
- Can you confirm root cause and whether this was a capacity routing or model-serving issue?
- What compensation will Redwood provide for the customer and for the overage costs we incurred?
- We’d like a short call today (window: 14:00–16:00 PT) if possible.

This is high priority for our ops and procurement teams — please advise next steps.

Thanks,
Aditi Sharma
Head of Platform Engineering
Novaflow

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: EXEC: Novaflow latency incident — request for concession approval

Team — following up from Aditi at Novaflow (details above). Quick summary of our preliminary findings:
- Incident window: 2027-06-27 03:15–03:50 UTC.
- Symptom: P95 jump to ~1.2s for ~18% of requests on Novaflow prod.
- Probable cause (initial): Router queuing during a transient KV-cache eviction coupled with a small routing imbalance on the N.California pool; not yet fully validated.
- Customer impact: retries and UX regressions; they estimate elevated downstream costs for retry traffic.

Customer asks remediation/credit. My recommendation for an approvable path (needs sign-off):
Option A (preferred): One month of committed-capacity credit (covering July) + $12,000 one-time credit applied to next invoice.
Option B: 20% invoice credit for June usage (estimated $9k).

Rationale for Option A: preserves relationship, minimizes churn risk, and buys us time to deploy the routing patch with a follow-up architecture review.

Attachments: incident_postmortem_summary.md

Can Marissa/LAUREN/Karthik indicate tolerance for each option and whether Finance/RevOps needs a reduced figure for precedent? I’ll coordinate customer comms once we have an approved amount.

Thanks,
Jonas

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 14:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EXEC: Novaflow latency incident — request for concession approval

Appreciate the quick triage, Jonas. I reviewed the initial postmortem and the customer report. Two quick notes on risk/precedent:
- We should avoid making an open-ended credit offer; any concession must be one-off and labeled as "goodwill" with an approval record in HubSpot.
- Finance will want a firm dollar cap and rationale. Lauren, can you confirm whether we can approve up to $12k on a discretionary basis or if we require Director-level approval?

Suggested compromise (to propose to the customer):
- One free month of their committed capacity applied to July (this addresses their immediate commercial ask).
- One-time credit capped at $8,000 applied to August invoice to cover measured overage/retry costs.
- Temporary SLA grace for scheduled routing patch work in July (we document exact maintenance windows).

This balances relationship protection and precedent. If Finance declines the $8k cap, we can fallback to a 25% credit for June’s bill (estimate in the $5–6k range).

Karthik — can you confirm the patch rollout ETA? If we can push the fix by 07/07, the operational waiver is reasonable.

-Marissa
Head, Revenue Operations
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

- If Marissa approves $8k cap, I’ll prioritize the rollout and designate an on-call lead for Novaflow for the week post-deploy.

Subject: Concession proposal and operational plan — Novaflow incident 2027-06-27

Aditi — thanks again for the patience while we investigated. We own the disruption and want to make this right. Below is the concession Redwood is prepared to extend as a one-time, non-precedent-setting goodwill offer: 

1) Commercial concession
- One free month of committed capacity, applied to your July billing cycle (covers your committed capacity fees for July).
- One-time credit of $7,500 to cover documented overage/retry costs, to be applied to your August invoice.

2) Operational commitments
- We will execute a staggered rollout of the routing/cache patch beginning 2027-07-03 and complete by 2027-07-06. Maintenance windows will be restricted to 02:00–05:00 UTC and we will notify you 48 hours in advance. Karthik’s team will provide an on-call escalation contact for the post-deploy week.

3) Scope and acceptance
- This offer is a one-off goodwill concession and does not modify the existing Master Service Agreement. Acceptance requires signing a short acknowledgement (DocuSign link below) confirming the concession and the maintenance windows.

If you accept, please sign here: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123DEF (concession_terms_docusign.pdf attached). Once signed, we’ll apply the credits to your account and schedule a joint architecture review.

Thanks — we value Novaflow as a strategic customer and want to ensure you’re stable for the remainder of the quarter.

Warmly,
Marissa Cole
